Paragraph:
Translation: Know that which pervades the entire body is indestructible. No one is able to destroy the imperishable soul.

Purport (Excerpt): This verse more clearly explains the real nature of the soul, which is spread all over the body. Anyone can understand what is spread all over the body: it is consciousness. Everyone is conscious of the pains and pleasures of the body in part or as a whole... Therefore, each and every body is the embodiment of an individual soul, and the symptom of the soul's presence is perceived as individual consciousness.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna needs tangible proof or a relatable concept to understand the abstract idea of an 'indestructible soul.'
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna identifies the soul by its symptom: consciousness. Just as the active principle of medicine spreads through the body, consciousness spreads from the localized soul (situated in the heart) throughout the entire physical form.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is given a practical way to perceive the spiritual reality within himself and others.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.mind-Body Connection: Understanding how the non-physical animates the physical

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Chetana (Consciousness, the observable symptom of the soul)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna provides the empirical evidence for the soul: consciousness. While the soul itself is atomic and invisible to material science, its presence is undeniable because it is the source of all bodily awareness (pains and pleasures). Since this consciousness stems from the indestructible spirit, the core self cannot be destroyed.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This encourages deep self-awareness. By identifying the 'self' not as the physical limbs or the brain, but as the underlying *consciousness* that feels and observes, an individual can detach from physical trauma. The body may be injured, but the observing consciousness itself remains whole and untouchable.
